### [We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/17/we-tracked-a-shipment-of-rare-books-it-ended-at-an-amazon-ai-tra/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-17

A 404 Media investigation used an Apple AirTag to track a 1,000-book marketplace purchase directly to an Amazon facility conducting destructive book scanning for AI training.

- A bookseller placed an Apple AirTag inside a 1,000-book order placed on the Biblio marketplace by an anonymous, price-insensitive buyer.
- The AirTag tracked the shipment to the VGT3 section of Amazon's LAS8 facility in northeast Las Vegas.
- Amazon worker forum discussions confirmed that the VGT3 location performs high-volume destructive book scanning.

**Why it matters:** The tracking provides concrete evidence of large-scale physical book acquisition and destructive scanning operations by major tech companies to build AI training datasets.

### [Don't classify. Hallucinate!](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/14/dont-classify-hallucinate/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-14

Doug Turnbull proposes assigning tags from large vocabularies to content by asking LLMs to generate freeform categories and matching those predictions to existing tags using vector embeddings.

- Large tag sets (such as 1,856 tags) exceed reasonable prompt context limits for direct classification.
- Prompting the model to generate hypothetical tags without showing it the existing vocabulary bypasses prompt size constraints.
- Vector embeddings map the model's generated tags against the existing tag corpus to identify the closest concrete matches.
- Prompts can include structural examples of desired classification shapes to guide the model's unconstrained output.

**Why it matters:** This technique allows systems to categorize content against massive, pre-existing taxonomies without exceeding context windows or degrading LLM classification accuracy.

`llms` `embeddings` `classification` `search` `generative-ai`
